follow-up time: The study period was from January to December 2020, although the exact duration of follow-up for each participant within this period isn't specified.
exposure: Gestational age: within 20 weeks, 30-34 weeks, and pre-delivery period (36 weeks or any time before preterm delivery)
Venous thromboembolism risk (according to Japanese guidelines)
Postpartum risk factors: high, intermediate, low, and none (based on Japanese guidelines)
cohort: 1026 women who delivered at 22-41 weeks of gestation at The University of Tsukuba Hospital, Japan, between January and December 2020
finding: The study found that a screening approach involving risk assessment, D-dimer testing, and ultrasonography was useful for identifying cases of deep vein thrombosis during pregnancy, particularly in the first trimester.
